title: Adonijah
lead: David's fourth son, born at Hebron to Haggith, who tried to make himself king in David's old age and lost the throne to Solomon. When he later asked for Abishag, Solomon had him killed.

sections.b: Adonijah is listed among the sons born to David at Hebron, the son of Haggith (2 Samuel 3:4; 1 Chronicles 3:2). With Amnon and Absalom dead, and nothing more said of Chileab, he seems to have been the oldest surviving son. In David's last days he declares "I will be king," gathers chariots and runners, wins over Joab and Abiathar, and holds a sacrificial feast at En-rogel, but Nathan, Bathsheba, Zadok and Benaiah act first and Solomon is anointed (1 Kings 1:5–40). He takes hold of the altar and is spared (1 Kings 1:50–53). After David's death his request for Abishag costs him his life (1 Kings 2:13–25). Chronicles leaves the whole struggle out. A Levite named Adonijah in 2 Chronicles 17:8 is a different man.
